newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Hui Shung passes on 54,500T soy/corn tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Hui Shung passes on 54,500T soy/corn tender.

text.p: Taiwan's Hui Shung Group on Thursday passed on a tender for a combined shipment comprising 38,500 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn due to high prices, traders said.
Traders said a retender could be scheduled before Taiwan's importers close up shop on February for the weeklong Chinese New Year holiday. Hui Shung's buyers would not comment.
Local traders said Hui Shung passed on the tender mainly due to rising offer prices for soybeans.
"Offers for soybeans moved up more than one U.S. dollar in just one day," a trader said, comparing Thursday's prices with those offered on Wednesday in a similar Taiwan soy tender.
Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association had passed on its tender on Wednesday for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, finding that Kanematsu's low offer of US$315.29 per tonne was too high.
No plans to retender for the shipment were announced.
The Hui Shung Group includes Hui Shung Agriculture and Food Corp, Eagle Food Industry and Charoen Pokphand.
Best offer for the corn segment of the tender was from Kanematsu at US$145.08 or 96.08 US cents per tonne over March Chicago futures, traders said.
Best offer for the soybean portion also was from Kanematsu at US$316.49 or 113.10 US cents per tonne over March Chicago futures, traders said.
Freight cost offers ranged between US$22.50 to US$23 per tonne, they said.
